content.text: JavaScript is required Skip to main content Mars Climate OrbiterMars Climate OrbiterDesigned to study Mars from orbit and serve as a communications relay for the Mars Polar Lander and Deep Space probes, the Mars Climate Orbiter was unsuccessful due to a navigation error caused by a failure to translate English units to metric.Mission StatisticsLaunch DateDec. 11, 1998Type OrbiterTarget MarsStatus PastAbout the missionDesigned to study Mars from orbit and serve as a communications relay for the Mars Polar Lander and Deep Space probes, the Mars Climate Orbiter was unsuccessful due to a navigation error caused by a failure to translate English units to metric.Last contact with the spacecraft was on September 23, 1999, 9 months after launch, and an investigation found that the spacecraft burned up in Mars' atmosphere.InstrumentsMars Color Imager (MARCI)Pressure Modulated Infrared Radiometer (PMIRR)Press Kit (PDF)Mars Climate Orbiter Information on Solar System ExplorationMars Climate Orbiter Information on National Space Science Data Center
